note: What the measured tool DECLARES, as the complete-meaning rule reads it: the terms a person may use for what the tool reads (subjects, metrics, targets), the shapes it reads, and whether it executes sampling. Neither profile declares sampling. 'declared-from-existing' was derived from the existing corpus only: every content word of its rows labelled reads or none had to be accounted for, and the words that name what a node-metrics tool reads became its terms. The held-out phrases were known when this file was written, so 'plus-held-out-nouns' exists to show the rule's cost when the tool also declares the metric and target nouns those phrases use. It adds nouns only, never a word that restricts a read. Adding terms can only turn asks into reads, so wrong readings are checked under the richer profile too. Neither profile declares the shape current, so a request for the current state asks.
